newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Woodside sees Laminaria contract soon.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Woodside sees Laminaria contract soon.

text.p: Woodside Petroleum Ltd said on Friday it expects to award a A$500 million contract for design and project management of a floating production vessel for the offshore Laminaria oilfield before Christmas.
A Woodside spokesman said he was unable to confirm the contract will be awarded to Kvaerner Oil & Gas, a part of Norway's Kvaerner ASA group.
However, sources close to the project said Kvaerner has already been chosen to head the project, with the Monaco-based Single Buoy Mooring group working with Kvaerner on a joint venture basis.
Single Buoy Mooring performed work on the construction of Woodside's one-sixth owned Cossack Pioneer offshore oil platform in Australia's North West Shelf.

The Woodside spokesman said the company was awaiting joint approval for a production license for Laminaria from the Australian and Northern Territory governments before making an offical announcement of the winning contract.
"I understand there are a couple of issues they are still discussing, but basically they have said we will have the license," the Woodside spokesman said.

"If we don't have it by the end of next week and it looks like it's going to be delayed until after Christmas, then we'll have to consider making an announcement about the contracts before then," he said.
A Norwegian newspaper last week reported that Kvaerner had managed to "shake off" rival group Brown & Root Inc of the U.S. in the final bidding round for the project.

The single-largest component of the project, a sub-contract with Korea's Samsung Heavy Industries Co Ltd valued at about A$300 million to design and construct a hull for the vessel, has already been announced.
"We needed to announce that earlier because we needed to secure yard space," the spokesman said.
Separate contracts valued at about A$200 million for the sub-sea components of the project, including flow heads and well heads, will also be announced before Christmas, the spokesman said.
"The total project is going to end up being close to the A$1 billion mark, he said.
Woodside has said it expects to begin production of oil from the Laminaria field by early 1999 at an average rate of 140,000 barrels a day.
Woodside holds a 50 percent stake in the project.
Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd and Royal/Dutch Shell each have 25 percent interests.
